arxiv-1811-05588.title: YOLO-LITE: A Real-Time Object Detection Algorithm Optimized for Non-GPU Computers *equal authorship
arxiv-1811-05588.creator: Rachel Huang *, Jonathan Pedoeem *, Cuixian Chen
arxiv-1811-05588.description: Abstract This paper focuses on YOLO-LITE, a real-time object detection model developed to run on portable devices such as a laptop or cellphone lacking a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). The model was first trained on the PASCAL VOC dataset then on the COCO dataset, achieving a mAP of 33.81% and 12.26% respectively.

arxiv-1903-05878.title: A Functional (Monadic) Second-Order Theory of Infinite Trees
arxiv-1903-05878.creator: Anupam Das, Colin Riba
arxiv-1903-05878.description: Abstract . This paper presents a complete axiomatization of Monadic Second-Order Logic ( 𝖬𝖲𝖮 \mathsf{MSO} ) over infinite trees. 𝖬𝖲𝖮 \mathsf{MSO} on infinite trees is a rich system, and its decidability (“Rabin’s Tree Theorem”) is one of the most powerful known results concerning the decidability of logics.

arxiv-2010-07807.title: Some properties of the torsion function with Robin boundary conditions
arxiv-2010-07807.creator: Rossano Sannipoli
arxiv-2010-07807.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Rossano Sannipoli. In this paper we study some properties of the torsion function with Robin boundary conditions. Here we write the shape derivative of the L ∞ L^{\infty} and L p L^{p} norms, for p ≥ 1 p\geq 1 , of the torsion function, seen as a functional on a bounded simply connected open set Ω ⊂ ℝ n \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n} , and prove that the balls are critical shapes for these functionals, when the volume of Ω \Omega is preserved.

arxiv-2104-11363.title: Nematicity Liquid in a Trimerized-Kagome Antiferromagnet
arxiv-2104-11363.creator: Ichiro Tanaka and Hirokazu Tsunetsugu
arxiv-2104-11363.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ichiro Tanaka and Hirokazu Tsunetsugu. We theoretically study low-temperature properties of the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model with half-integer spin S S on the kagome lattice with large trimerization. We have derived a low-energy effective model for general S S in terms of spin and nematicity operators in triangular units, and studied their low-temperature correlations for S S = 3 / 2 3/2 by classical Monte Carlo simulations. The previous study for the S S = 1 / 2 1/2 case [M.

X

arxiv-2209-02462.title: Rethinking the Memory Staleness Problem in Dynamics GNN
arxiv-2209-02462.creator: Mor Ventura, Hadas Ben Atya, Dekel Brav
arxiv-2209-02462.description: Abstract The staleness problem is a well-known problem when working with dynamic data, due to the absence of events for a long time. Since the memory of the node is updated only when the node is involved in an event, the i’s memory becomes stale.

arxiv-2210-04505.title: A Survey on Heterogeneous Federated Learning
arxiv-2210-04505.creator: Dashan Gao, Xin Yao, and Qiang Yang
arxiv-2210-04505.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL) has been proposed to protect data privacy and virtually assemble the isolated data silos by cooperatively training models among organizations without breaching privacy and security. However, FL faces heterogeneity from various aspects, including data space, statistical, and system heterogeneity.

arxiv-2301-04054.title: Surface-Sensitive Raman Scattering by Transferable Nanoporous Plasmonic Membranes
arxiv-2301-04054.creator: Roman M. Wyss, Günter Kewes, Martin Frimmer, Karl-Philipp Schlichting, Markus Parzefall, Eric Bonvin, Martin F. Sarott, Morgan Trassin, Lala Habibova, Giorgia Marcelli, Jan Vermant, Lukas Novotny, Mads C. Weber, Sebastian Heeg
arxiv-2301-04054.description: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is a powerful technique to characterize materials. It probes non-destructively chemical composition, crystallinity, defects, strain and coupling phenomena. However, the Raman response of surfaces or thin films is often weak and obscured by dominant bulk signals. Here we overcome this limitation by placing a transferable porous gold membrane (PAuM) on top of the surface of interest.

arxiv-2306-12072.title: Collective effects enhanced multi-qubit information engines
arxiv-2306-12072.creator: Noufal Jaseem, Victor Mukherjee
arxiv-2306-12072.description: Abstract We study a quantum information engine (QIE) modeled by a multi-qubit working medium (WM) collectively coupled to a single thermal bath. We show that one can harness the collective effects to significantly enhance the performance of the QIE, as compared to equivalent engines lacking collective effects.

arxiv-2311-04992.title: Depth resolved study of annealing in IrMn/(Fe, Co, CoFe) exchange bias systems
arxiv-2311-04992.creator: Yu. Khaydukov, A. Dobrynin, S. Hassan, M. Ormston, K. Nikolaev, P. Bencok, R. Fan, P. Steadman, A. Csik, A. Vorobiev
arxiv-2311-04992.description: Abstract Depth resolved study of structural and magnetic profiles of antiferromagnetic/ferromagnetic (AFM/FM) system upon annealing was performed in this work. We studied systems comprising of AFM IrMn and FM (Co, Fe, Co 70 Fe 30 ) structures using polarized neutron and soft X-ray scattering, secondary neutral spectrometry, and magnetometry.

arxiv-2312-09813.title: Machine Learning Applications in Astrophysics: Photometric Redshift Estimation
arxiv-2312-09813.creator: John Y. H. Soo, Ishaq Yahya Khalfan Al Shuaili, Imdad Mahmud Pathi
arxiv-2312-09813.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by John Y. H. Soo, Ishaq Yahya Khalfan Al Shuaili, Imdad Mahmud Pathi. Machine learning has rose to become an important research tool in the past decade, its application has been expanded to almost if not all disciplines known to mankind. Particularly, the use of machine learning in astrophysics research had a humble beginning in the early 1980s, it has rose and become widely used in many sub-fields today, driven by the vast availability of free astronomical data online.

arxiv-2507-13209.title: Reconstructing Air-Shower Observables using a Universality-Based Model at the Pierre Auger Observatory
arxiv-2507-13209.creator: Maximilian Stadelmaier
arxiv-2507-13209.description: Abstract Based on solutions of the cascade equations, the air-shower universality is a framework that for all air showers with the same energy, zenith angle, depth of shower maximum, and muon number predicts the same longitudinal, lateral, and energy distributions of electromagnetic shower particles.

europmc-pmc7403393.title: In vitro screening of a FDA approved chemical library reveals potential inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 replication.
europmc-pmc7403393.creator: Touret F, Gilles M, Barral K, Nougairède A, van Helden J, Decroly E, de Lamballerie X, Coutard B.
europmc-pmc7403393.description: A novel coronavirus, named SARS-CoV-2, emerged in 2019 in China and rapidly spread worldwide. As no approved therapeutics exists to treat COVID-19, the disease associated to SARS-Cov-2, there is an urgent need to propose molecules that could quickly enter into clinics....

plos-pone-0359208.description: A reliability analysis method for Christmas tree in operating conditions based on FEMCA, FTA and numerical simulation

pmc-10701872.title: COVID-19 ORF3a Viroporin-Influenced Common and Unique Cellular Signaling Cascades in Lung, Heart, and the Brain Choroid Plexus Organoids with Additional Enriched MicroRNA Network Analyses for Lung and the Brain Tissues
pmc-10701872.creator: Soura Chakraborty, Shrabonti Chatterjee, Subhashree Mardi, Joydeep Mahata, Suneel Kateriya, Pradeep Punnakkal, Gireesh Anirudhan
pmc-10701872.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Tissue-specific implications of SARS-CoV-2-encoded accessory proteins are not fully understood. SARS-CoV-2 infection can severely affect three major organs—the heart, lungs, and brain. We analyzed SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a interacting host proteins in these three major organs. Furthermore, we identified common and unique interacting host proteins and their targeting miRNAs (lung and brain) and delineated associated biological processes by reanalyzing RNA-seq data from the brain (COVID-19-infected/uninfected choroid plexus organoid study), lung tissue from COVID-19 patients/healthy subjects, and cardiomyocyte cells-based transcriptomics analyses.

pmc-10770689.title: Class I HLA Allele Predicted Restricted Antigenic Coverages for Fap2 Protein of Fusobacterium Nucleatum Are Associated with Colorectal Cancer Incidence
pmc-10770689.creator: Mustapha Zeddou
pmc-10770689.description: Objective:This study investigates the association between HLA-A and -B allele diversity, Fusobacterium nucleatum Fap2 protein-derived antigenic coverage, and colorectal cancer (CRC) epidemiology across diverse populations.Methods:We examined 75 HLA-I alleles and explored 698 potential HLA-A and B-restricted Fap2-derived antigens, assessing how 21 countries may respond to these peptides based on their HLA-I distribution frequencies.

pmc-11269366.title: Factors that influence the angular error in active knee angle reproduction tests: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
pmc-11269366.creator: Juliane Wieber, Leon Müller‐Rahmel, Rüdiger Reer, Robert Rein, Bjoern Braunstein
pmc-11269366.description: PurposeThe systematic review and meta‐analysis investigated subject‐independent test factors that influence the absolute angle error in active knee angle reproduction tests.MethodsFive electronic databases were searched to identify relevant studies published before 20 December 2023. Studies were included that were published in either English or German and that investigated joint proprioception in the healthy knee.

pmc-11312486.title: Additional Value of Ultrasound in Patients with Psoriatic Arthritis within Treatment Target
pmc-11312486.creator: Mihaela Agache, Claudiu C Popescu, Luminița Enache, Corina Mogoșan, Emilio Filippucci, Cătălin Codreanu, Santos Castañeda
pmc-11312486.description: Background: In psoriatic arthritis (PsA), musculoskeletal ultrasound is a complementary tool to physical examination, useful even in patients in remission to detect subclinical activity. Objectives: The objective of the study was to assess the ultrasound prevalence of active enthesitis and synovitis in patients who reached the therapeutic target.

pmc-11429122.title: The Proteasome-Family-Members-Based Prognostic Model Improves the Risk Classification for Adult Acute Myeloid Leukemia
pmc-11429122.creator: Guangying Sheng, Jingfen Tao, Peng Jin, Yilu Li, Wen Jin, Kankan Wang, Christos K Kontos, Myunggon Ko
pmc-11429122.description: Background: The accumulation of diverse molecular and cytogenetic variations contributes to the heterogeneity of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), a cluster of hematologic malignancies that necessitates enhanced risk evaluation for prognostic prediction and therapeutic guidance. The ubiquitin–proteasome system plays a crucial role in AML; however, the specific contributions of 49 core proteasome family members (PSMs) in this context remain largely unexplored.

pmc-11440718.title: Impact of social, familial and personal factors on depressive symptoms in middle-aged and older adults from the national CHARLS cohort
pmc-11440718.creator: Xiaoqian Zhang, Mei Xue, Zifeng Zhang, Ziyu Gao, Chunyan Li, Jing Wu, Wenquan Niu
pmc-11440718.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to evaluate whether social, familial and personal factors can predict incident and prevalent depressive symptoms in Chinese adults aged ≥ 45 years using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).MethodsStudy subjects without depressive symptoms from CHARLS at baseline were enrolled. Depressive symptoms were defined by the 10-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale.

pmc-12735341.title: A Study on Visible Light Communication Systems Based on OLED Devices
pmc-12735341.creator: Wanyi Zhang, Haochen Xu, Sihang Ji, Jiazhuang Lan, Jing Wei, Fangze Liu
pmc-12735341.description: Addressing the limitations of conventional inorganic light-emitting diodes (LEDs) in flexible visible light communication (VLC) applications, this study investigates the feasibility of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) as an integrated platform for illumination, display, and communication. The optoelectronic characteristics and modulation bandwidth of red, green, and blue (RGB) OLEDs were systematically measured.

pmc-13352080.title: Clinical expressions, disease course, quality of life, and resilience in subgroups of patients with angioedema☆
pmc-13352080.creator: Iris Leibovich-Nassi, Avner Reshef, Michal Itzhaki
pmc-13352080.description: ObjectivePatients with angioedema caused by C1INH deficiency (HAE-C1INH) experience recurrent episodes of unpredictable swelling. Recently, new genetic variants have been identified, whereas patients with unknown causes and no identifiable genetic mutations constitute a distinct subgroup. As a lifelong condition, angioedema significantly impacts the patient's quality of life and ability to cope.

pmc-13355474.title: Scoping Review of Polygenic Risk Scores in Kidney-Related Traits
pmc-13355474.creator: Yuka Sugawara, Kaoru Ito, Masao Iwagami, Ryota Inokuchi, Yoshihito Nihei, Masaomi Nangaku, Yosuke Hirakawa
pmc-13355474.description: IntroductionLarge-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous loci associated with various diseases and traits, enabling the development of polygenic risk scores (PRS) and genetic risk scores (GRS) that capture cumulative effects of variants. Although these scores have been applied in nephrology, no review has systematically evaluated their implementation or performance.

pmc-13360452.title: Glycemic variability does not provide incremental prognostic value for in-hospital death in community-acquired pneumonia patients: conventional clinical variables dominate
pmc-13360452.creator: Jiaojiao Zhou, Kaiyu Cai, Yinggang Zhu, Yanchun Gong, Haiyan Ge, Hua Sheng
pmc-13360452.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to systematically evaluate whether glycemic variability (GV) could provide independent incremental prognostic value for in-hospital death among patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), beyond conventional clinical variables including the SOFA score.MethodsData were retrieved from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database, with a multicenter intensive care unit (ICU) database used as the external validation set.
